questions.question: A train of length 300 metres crosses a tree in 20 seconds and crosses another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of the first train = Distance ÷ Time = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 m/s

Relative speed of both trains (opposite direction) = Total Distance ÷ Time = (300 + 300) ÷ 25 = 600 ÷ 25 = 24 m/s

Speed of the second train = Relative Speed − Speed of first train = 24 − 15 = 9 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 9 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7fe2cb9f8b0b10992f5f16c8700501c9f9a876b4fdc5916368e2d0baba0e4e17.png] 

**Given:**

Length of Train 1 (L₁) = 300 m

Time to cross a tree = 20 s

Length of Train 2 (L₂) = 300 m

Time to cross each other = 25 s

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 m/s

⇒ Total distance to cross each other = L₁ + L₂ = 300 + 300 = 600 m

⇒ Relative speed = Total Distance ÷ Crossing Time

⇒ S₁ + S₂ = 600 ÷ 25

⇒ 15 + S₂ = 24

⇒ S₂ = 24 − 15

⇒ S₂ = 9 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 9 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two trains travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: S = S₁ − S₂ (where S₁ > S₂).

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two trains travel towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: S = S₁ + S₂.

Crossing a Stationary Object

If a train crosses a pole, standing man, or tree, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train alone: D = L₁.

Crossing a Platform/Bridge

If a train crosses a platform or another train, the total distance covered is the sum of their lengths: D = L₁ + L₂.
</p

questions.question: The sum of the length and breadth of a cuboid is 4 cm. Length is three times of breadth. If the height of the cuboid is half of the sum of the length and breadth, then what is total surface of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Length** to **Breadth** = 3 : 1 ⇒ Sum = 4 units.

Given 4 units = 4 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 1 cm, so **L = 3 cm** and **B = 1 cm**.

**Height (H)** = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm.

**Total Surface Area** = 2(LB + BH + HL) = 2(3×1 + 1×2 + 2×3) = 2 × 11 = 22 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 22 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Sum of **Length (L)** and **Breadth (B)** = 4 cm

⇒ **Length (L)** = 3 × **Breadth (B)**

⇒ **Height (H)** = 1/2 × (L + B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/adddee43c7b983c3dc61bb6f41420ff4d81bb95e424c778ccc32c9397fd525d7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ L + B = 4

⇒ 3B + B = 4

⇒ 4B = 4 ⇒ **B = 1 cm**

⇒ L = 3 × 1 = **3 cm**

⇒ H = 4 ÷ 2 = **2 cm**

⇒ **Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2(LB + BH + HL)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (3 × 1 + 1 × 2 + 2 × 3)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (3 + 2 + 6) = 2 × 11 = 22 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 22 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by a cuboid is given by the formula: **Volume = L × B × H**.

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four vertical faces of the cuboid is: **LSA = 2 × H × (L + B)**.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is: **D = √(L² + B² + H²)**.</p

questions.question: In what ratio tea of Rs. 60 per kg should be mixed with tea of Rs. 70 per kg so that on selling the mixture at Rs. 80 per kg there is a profit of 25 percent?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **Cost Price (CP)** of the mixture: CP = 80 × (100 / 125) = ₹64.

Apply the **Alligation Rule** directly with the three Cost Prices (60, 70, and 64).

Ratio = (70 − 64) : (64 − 60) = 6 : 4 = 3 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price of first variety (**CP₁**) = ₹60 per kg

Cost Price of second variety (**CP₂**) = ₹70 per kg

Selling Price of mixture (**SPₘᵢₓ**) = ₹80 per kg

**Profit percentage** = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price = [Selling Price × 100] / [100 + Profit %]

Alligation Ratio (Cheaper : Dearer) = (CPDₑₐᵣₑᵣ − CPMₑₐₙ) : (CPMₑₐₙ − CPCₕₑₐₚₑᵣ)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/56f5f24f0bfab9de0a21cdf30a04703f84771bdc15ea26ae5c7728cd5ddcd6b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean CP = [80 × 100] / [100 + 25]

⇒ Mean CP = [80 × 100] / 125

⇒ Mean CP = 80 × (4 / 5)

⇒ Mean CP = 16 × 4 = ₹64 per kg

⇒ Using Alligation method:

⇒ (Quantity of ₹60 tea) / (Quantity of ₹70 tea) = (70 − 64) / (64 − 60)

⇒ Ratio = 6 / 4 = 3 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired **Mean Price**. All values must be in the same unit (all CP or all SP).

Mean Price Calculation

The **Mean Price** is always the **Cost Price** of the mixture. If the selling price and profit percentage are given, the CP must be calculated before applying alligation.

Profit and Loss Relation

When profit occurs, **SP = CP × (1 + P/100)**. When loss occurs, **SP = CP × (1 − L/100)**.

questions.question: The average marks obtained by 120 students in an examination is 50. If the average marks of passed students is 70 and average marks of the failed students is 30, then what is the number of students who passed the examination?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Average marks of 120 students = 50.

Average marks of passed students = 70.

Average marks of failed students = 30

**Formula:**

Total marks = number of students * average marks

**Solution:**

⇒ Total marks of 120 students = 120 * 50 = 6000.

⇒ Let the number of students who passed be x.

⇒ Total marks of passed students + total marks of failed students = Total marks of all students.

⇒ 70x + 30(120-x) = 6000.

⇒ 40x = 2400.

⇒ x = 2400 / 40 = 60.

**Therefore, the number of students who passed the examination is 60.**

questions.question: A seller allows a discount of 9% on a watch. If he allows a discount of 6%, he earns Rs. 30 more in profit. What is the marked price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in the given discount percentages = 9% − 6% = 3%

The difference in profit corresponds exactly to the difference in the discount amount.

⇒ 3% of Marked Price = Rs. 30

⇒ Marked Price = 30 × (100 ÷ 3) = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Discount = 9%

New Discount = 6%

Increase in profit = Rs. 30

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) − Discount

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price (CP)

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 MP

 
 SP2 (6% off)

 
 SP1 (9% off)
 
 
 

 

 6% off

 
 

 

 3% diff = Rs. 30

 
 

 9% Total Discount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Marked Price = MP and Cost Price = CP

⇒ Selling Price in Case 1 (SP₁) = MP − 9% of MP = 0.91 MP

⇒ Profit in Case 1 = 0.91 MP − CP

⇒ Selling Price in Case 2 (SP₂) = MP − 6% of MP = 0.94 MP

⇒ Profit in Case 2 = 0.94 MP − CP

⇒ Difference in profit = Profit in Case 2 − Profit in Case 1

⇒ (0.94 MP − CP) − (0.91 MP − CP) = 30

⇒ 0.03 MP = 30

⇒ MP = 30 ÷ 0.03 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is an allowance given to the buyer on the catalog price. It is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single effective discount is calculated using the formula: (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Profit and Loss Baseline

Unlike discounts which are based on Marked Price, profit or loss is inherently always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise.

questions.question: If sin m + sin n = p, cos m + cos n = q, then find the value of sin m × sin n + cos m × cos n.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sin m + sin n = p

cos m + cos n = q

**Concept Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculation:**

sin m + sin n = p

Square both sides

(sin m + sin n)² = p²

1 - cos2 m + 1 - cos2 n + 2 × sin m × sin n = p² ................(i)

cos m + cos n = q

Square both sides

cos2 m + cos2 n + 2 × cos m × cos n = q2................(ii)

Add equation (i) and (ii)

2 + 2 × sin m × sin n + 2 × cos m × cos n = q² + p2

2(sin m × sin n + cos m × cos n) = q2 + p² - 2

sin m × sin n + cos m × cos n = (q2 + p2 - 2)/2

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A certain sum becomes 4 times of itself in 5 years at a rate of simple interest. In 15 years it will become how many times of itself at the same rate of simple interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In Simple Interest, the interest earned is directly proportional to the time period.

Direct Formula: (n₁ − 1) ÷ t₁ = (n₂ − 1) ÷ t₂

Given: n₁ = 4, t₁ = 5 years, t₂ = 15 years.

⇒ (4 − 1) ÷ 5 = (n₂ − 1) ÷ 15

⇒ 3 ÷ 5 = (n₂ − 1) ÷ 15 ⇒ n₂ − 1 = 9 ⇒ n₂ = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A sum becomes 4 times of itself in 5 years at simple interest.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 
 
 

 
 

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 

 P
 4P
 7P
 10P

 0 Yrs
 5 Yrs
 10 Yrs
 15 Yrs

 

 

 

 + 3P (SI)
 + 3P (SI)
 + 3P (SI)

 Total Amount at 15 Years = 10P (10 times)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the principal sum be P.

⇒ Amount after 5 years = 4P

⇒ Simple Interest earned in 5 years = 4P − P = 3P

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

⇒ R = (3P × 100) ÷ (P × 5) = 60%

⇒ Now, we need to find the amount after T = 15 years at R = 60%:

⇒ SI = (P × 60 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 900P ÷ 100 = 9P

⇒ New Amount = Principal + SI = P + 9P = 10P

⇒ Thus, the sum will become 10 times of itself.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Constant Growth

Unlike compound interest, simple interest grows by a constant amount every year. If a sum earns 3P interest in 5 years, it will earn exactly 3P interest in every subsequent 5-year period.

Direct Formula for Multipliers

When a sum becomes n₁ times in t₁ years and n₂ times in t₂ years at simple interest, use the relation: (n₁ − 1) ÷ t₁ = (n₂ − 1) ÷ t₂.

Principal and Amount Relation

The amount (A) is the sum of Principal (P) and Simple Interest (SI). Always subtract 1 from the number of times it becomes to get the interest multiplier: SI = (n − 1)P.
</p

questions.question: O is the incentre of the ΔPQR. If ∠POR = 120 degree, then what is the ∠PQR?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

∠POR = 120 degree

**Formula:**

The incenter of a triangle is equally inclined to all the sides of the triangle.

Angle at incentre = 90° + vertex angle/2

**Solution:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e262e79f2c52b00ab525cddf698eb5eb72bac6d07a0e95f7c6bd562f5416e413.png] 

⇒ ∠POR = 120° 

⇒ ∠POR = 90° + ∠PQR/2

⇒ 120° = 90 + ∠PQR/2

⇒ ∠PQR/2 = 120 - 90

⇒ ∠PQR = 30° × 2 = 60° 

**Hence, ΔPQR is 60°. **

questions.question: What is the least possible value of p for which a number 84pp153p is divisible by 9?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **sum of digits** must be a multiple of 9.

Sum of digits of **84pp153p** = 8 + 4 + p + p + 1 + 5 + 3 + p = 21 + 3p.

Check for the smallest value of p from options: If **p = 2**, sum = 21 + 3(2) = 27.

Since 27 is divisible by 9, the least value of p is 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The number is **84pp153p** and it is divisible by 9.

**Formula Used:** For a number to be divisible by 9, the **sum of its digits** must be divisible by 9.

⇒ Sum of digits = 8 + 4 + p + p + 1 + 5 + 3 + p

⇒ Sum = 21 + 3p

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 9, (21 + 3p) should be 27, 36, 45, ...

⇒ Case 1: 21 + 3p = 27

⇒ 3p = 27 − 21

⇒ 3p = 6

⇒ p = 2

⇒ Case 2: 21 + 3p = 36

⇒ 3p = 15 ⇒ p = 5

⇒ Case 3: 21 + 3p = 45

⇒ 3p = 24 ⇒ p = 8

⇒ The possible values for p are 2, 5, and 8. The **least possible value** is 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9. Every number divisible by 9 is also divisible by 3.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the **sum of digits at odd places** and the **sum of digits at even places** is either 0 or a multiple of 11.</p

questions.question: If m² - n² = 21 and m - n = 3, find the value of m + n.
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

m² - n² = 21

m - n = 3

**Formula:**

The difference of squares: a² - b² = (a+b)(a-b)

**Solution:**

⇒ m² - n² = (m+n)(m-n) = 21.

⇒ As m - n = 3, m + n = 21/3 = 7.

**Therefore, the value of m + n is 7.**

questions.question: P's income is 150 percent of Q's income and P's expenditure is 60 percent of Q's expenditure. If Q saves 20 percent of his income, then how much percentage does P save of his own income?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Q's Income** = 100 → **Q's Savings** = 20 → **Q's Expenditure** = 80.

**P's Income** = 150% of 100 = 150.

**P's Expenditure** = 60% of 80 = 48.

**P's Savings** = 150 − 48 = 102.

**P's Saving Percentage** = (102 ÷ 150) × 100 = 68%.

**∴ The correct answer is 68%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Income** of **P** = 150% of **Income** of **Q**

**Expenditure** of **P** = 60% of **Expenditure** of **Q**

**Savings** of **Q** = 20% of his **Income**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e93b5c89e7882cde673acf1b95c452167e22935c85c115c422ec55149ac6b44.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let **Income** of **Q** = 100x

⇒ **Savings** of **Q** = 20% of 100x = 20x

⇒ **Expenditure** of **Q** = 100x − 20x = 80x

⇒ **Income** of **P** = 150% of 100x = 150x

⇒ **Expenditure** of **P** = 60% of 80x = 48x

⇒ **Savings** of **P** = **Income** of **P** − **Expenditure** of **P**

⇒ **Savings** of **P** = 150x − 48x = 102x

⇒ **P's Savings Percentage** = (102x ÷ 150x) × 100

⇒ **P's Savings Percentage** = (102 ÷ 1.5) = 68%

**∴ The correct answer is 68%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Income Formula

Income = Expenditure + Savings. This is the fundamental equation for all budget-related problems.

Savings Percentage

Savings % = (Savings ÷ Income) × 100. This measures what portion of the total earnings is retained after expenses.

Ratio of Income & Expenditure

If the ratio of **Income**, **Expenditure**, and **Savings** is known for one person, it can be scaled using multipliers to compare with another person.</p

questions.question: If a + b = 24 and 8ab = 256, then what is the value of 3a² + 3b²?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

a + b = 24

8ab = 256

**Formula:**

The square of the sum of two numbers is equal to the sum of their squares plus twice their product (a+b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Solution:**

⇒ ab = 256/8 = 32.

⇒ (a+b)² = 24² = 576.

⇒ a² + b² = (a+b)² - 2ab = 576 - 64 = 512.

⇒ 3a² + 3b² = 3(a² + b²) = 3*512 = 1536.

**Therefore, the value of 3a² + 3b² is 1536.**

questions.question: A alone can make a table in 30 days while B alone can make it in 15 days. B started the work alone and worked for 8 days. In how many days A alone can finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(30, 15) = 30 units

Efficiency of A = 30 ÷ 30 = 1 unit/day, B = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units/day

Work done by B in 8 days = 8 × 2 = 16 units

Remaining work = 30 − 16 = 14 units

Time taken by A alone = 14 ÷ 1 = 14 days

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A alone = 30 days

Time taken by B alone = 15 days

B worked alone for 8 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 30

 2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by B in 8 days = Efficiency of B × Days

⇒ Work done by B = 2 × 8 = 16 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done by B

⇒ Remaining work = 30 − 16 = 14 units

⇒ Time taken by A to complete remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A = 14 ÷ 1 = 14 days

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a piece of work in x days and B can do it in y days, then both working together can complete it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of work done by each individual. If they work for the same duration, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When two people work on alternate days, calculate the total work done in a 2-day cycle. Then multiply this cycle to get as close to the total work as possible without exceeding it.
</p

questions.question: If 6x = 3y = 2z, then what is the value of (1)/(y)+(1)/(z)-(1)/(x)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate all parts to a constant **k**: 6x = 3y = 2z = k.

Express **bases** in terms of k: 6 = k¹/x, 3 = k¹/y, and 2 = k¹/z.

Use the mathematical relation: **6 = 3 × 2**.

Substitute k: k¹/x = k¹/y × k¹/z ⇒ k¹/x = k⁽¹/y ⁺ ¹/z⁾.

Comparing powers: 1/x = 1/y + 1/z ⇒ **1/y + 1/z − 1/x = 0**.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 6x = 3y = 2z

**Formula Used:** If am = b, then a = b¹/m; and am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61778689235d73c4449dad390b675e5ac57ebaeb02306e53c009c2173342be3f.png] 

⇒ Let 6x = 3y = 2z = k

⇒ 6 = k¹/x --- (i)

⇒ 3 = k¹/y --- (ii)

⇒ 2 = k¹/z --- (iii)

⇒ We know that 6 = 3 × 2

⇒ Substituting the values from (i), (ii), and (iii):

⇒ k¹/x = k¹/y × k¹/z

⇒ k¹/x = k⁽¹/y ⁺ ¹/z⁾

⇒ 1/x = 1/y + 1/z

⇒ 1/y + 1/z − 1/x = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of Exponents

When multiplying two powers with the same base, add the exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.

Power Conversion

To isolate a base, move the exponent to the other side as its reciprocal: if xa = y, then x = y¹/a.

Equality of Bases

If am = aⁿ and a ≠ 1, 0, or −1, then the exponents must be equal: m = n.</p

questions.question: What is the value of (cottheta+cosectheta - 1)/(cottheta - cosectheta +1)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put a specific value for **θ**, say **θ = 45°**, where **cot 45° = 1** and **cosec 45° = √2**.

Expression = (1 + √2 − 1) / (1 − √2 + 1) = √2 / (2 − √2)

Rationalize: √2 / [ √2(√2 − 1) ] = 1 / (√2 − 1) = **√2 + 1**.

Evaluating **(cosec θ + cot θ)** at 45°: √2 + 1. Both values match perfectly.

**∴ The correct answer is (cosec θ + cot θ).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The trigonometric expression (cot θ + cosec θ − 1) / (cot θ − cosec θ + 1).

**Formula Used:** We use the fundamental **trigonometric identity**: cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 and the **algebraic identity** a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6845a5d0df9730e69f09f9c4eb7841b71b775c68e1ef07d29063fa9161665398.png] 

⇒ [(cot θ + cosec θ) − (cosec²θ − cot²θ)] / (cot θ − cosec θ + 1)

⇒ [(cosec θ + cot θ) − (cosec θ − cot θ)(cosec θ + cot θ)] / (cot θ − cosec θ + 1)

⇒ {(cosec θ + cot θ) [1 − (cosec θ − cot θ)]} / (cot θ − cosec θ + 1)

⇒ {(cosec θ + cot θ) [1 − cosec θ + cot θ]} / (1 − cosec θ + cot θ)

⇒ Cancelling the common term (1 − cosec θ + cot θ) from numerator and denominator:

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ

**∴ The correct answer is (cosec θ + cot θ).**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Standard identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Property

The difference of squares yields (cosec θ − cot θ) = 1 / (cosec θ + cot θ).

Symmetry in Simplification

Similar expressions involving (tan θ + sec θ − 1) / (tan θ − sec θ + 1) simplify to (sec θ + tan θ).</p
